guardianfootball.description: It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances. Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk would not have been a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player? The reality is Tarkowski’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles, meaning there was always likely to come a time when his luck…

guardianfootball.description: Maximising the societal impact of the tournament, especially combating misogyny, should be a top priority The announcement that the 2035 Women’s World Cup will be hosted in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland has finally come and, if we aim high enough, it could have a massive societal impact. Confirmation was a foregone conclusion – the UK was the only bidder – but that did not mean the submission was complacent or lacked ambition. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show
guardianfootball.description: Management team were in line for huge payouts Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.description: ‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”. Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum…

guardianfootball.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
guardianfootball.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82…

guardianfootball.title: David Raya’s shoulder injury ‘not too serious’ and no surgery needed for Arsenal goalkeeper
guardianfootball.description: No 1 to miss Dortmund game but could return for City clash ‘We were worried … he’s better than expected,’ says manager Mikel Arteta is hopeful the ­shoulder injury David Raya sustained at Newcastle is not too serious, but confirmed the goalkeeper would miss Tuesday’s Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund. Raya was forced off in the ­second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw with a ­suspected dislocated shoulder, ­raising fears he could be sidelined for an extended period. He had an MRI scan on Arsenal’s return to London and was absent from ­training on Monday. Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise at home to Dortmund. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Jamal Musiala controversy the nadir of Bayern Munich’s turbulent week
guardianfootball.description: German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat. The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s…

guardianfootball.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
guardianfootball.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras…

pitchfork.title: Thanatos
pitchfork.description: Bradford Cox’s first solo album in 15 years is a haunted, autumnal meditation on all forms of decay: bodily, spiritual, political, and sonic.

pitchfork.title: Demoed EP
pitchfork.description: MJ Lenderman, Circuit des Yeux, Flock of Dimes, and more lend their voices to stripped-down versions of songs from this year’s Punching the Clown on a new EP that continues the remarkable transformation of Lambchop.

pitchfork.description: The Brooklyn and Delhi-based singer-songwriter tells stories of strange and solitary women cast out by society: murderers, sex workers, and schemers determined to secure their freedom by any means.

pitchfork.title: Glitter
pitchfork.description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the superstar’s infamous eighth album and film soundtrack, an effervescent blend of retro synth-pop, aughties hip-hop, and piano balladry with legendary baggage.

pitchfork.title: Reveal (25th Anniversary Edition)
pitchfork.description: The rock band’s sunny synth-pop pivot remains an undersung gem. On a new reissue, it also feels like a touchstone for the sound of indie-pop in the 21st century.

pitchfork.title: Live at the Barbican
pitchfork.description: Two years after her long-awaited solo debut, the Pixes/Breeders/Amps singer-songwriter returns with an opulent concert album that pushes her abundant personality to the fore.

pitchfork.title: Astro
pitchfork.description: The veteran Italian techno producer draws on the sounds of his childhood, transforming vintage anime anthems into a heady electronic odyssey.

pitchfork.title: MO LÉAN
pitchfork.description: Rose Connolly’s newly reissued second album explores suppressed Irish mourning customs. In her mix of electronic processing and traditional music, she uncovers a communal, expressive vision of grief.

quietus.title: Nikola Balberčáková on New Album and PAF Olomouc Appearance
quietus.description: Irina Shtreis talks to Nikola Balberčáková about her troubling AV piece r/ForeverAlone and the new work she will present in Olomouc this December Social media narratives may not be the easiest material to work with when creating convincing artwork. It can be hard to sift through layers of superfluous information. Genuine personal stories often get tangled up with attempts at creative writing. Despite potential pitfalls, Prague-based Slovakian artist Nikola Balberčáková delved into online forums in order to produce a critically-acclaimed audiovisual work called r/ForeverAlone. The 2024 project drew inspiration from the eponymous digital community on Reddit. The content on the titular…

quietus.description: Having delivered one of the most ambitious records of 2026 with last month's Dja Dja, the Catalan composer presents a 20-track playlist of the influences that fed into it, available exclusively for tQ Subscriber Plus tier members Photo by Silvio Deiaco, Danilo Gambara & Christian Kondić Music journalists love to declare the influences that must have gone into a new album, but often the artists themselves are left baffled by such comparisons. We thought, why not go straight to the source? Marina Herlop is a Catalan composer, vocalist and pianist, whose new album Dja Dja was self-released last month. Taking its structure from the archetypal Hero's Journey, the record took shape over three…

The project was initiated by Heart n Soul member, bandleader, composer,…

quietus.description: In an exclusive extract from his new book, The Full English: The Ways We Eat and Why, chef and sociologist Lewis Bassett looks at how a dish of 'French' style potatoes (actually Belgian) and imported haddock became a potent symbol of the British nation Photo: Andrew Dunn. I’m waiting for Graham at the train station when he messages to say he’s outside in a white pickup. This, as it turns out, is not the statement vehicle it is in London but a practical truck with room for a pallet of fish in the back. When I hop in, Graham, who is...

quietus.title: A Departure: Joni Mitchell’s Hejira at 50
quietus.description: Kat Lister looks at a radical shift in the 'open road' narrative as exemplified in Joni Mitchell's relatively overlooked eighth album In October of this year, a 17-person expedition voyaged 2,500 miles from the coastline of Papua New Guinea, to a remote Pacific lagoon, looking for Amelia Earhart’s lost aircraft. Satellite images some six years earlier had shown what was believed to be a submerged object with a metallic glint in shallow water. And the glint suggested something to the expedition’s leader, Richard Pettigrew, even if that “something” turned out to be illusory. Which it did. "You know, Amelia herself said, 'Adventure is worthwhile in itself',” he mused with reporters upon his…

It will be made available in a triple-vinyl edition, as well as in a crystal-clear triple-vinyl limited edition version. The new live album follows on from the 2021 release of The Comeback Special – Live At The Royal Albert Hall.…

Taking in 12 tracks, Clapton Hymns, Vol. 1 features recordings by Tortoise's Jeff Parker, Moses Boyd's Exodus and Collocutor, among others. Perhaps the standout, though, is a performance by Tony Allen of 'Never (Lagos Never Gonna Be The Same)', which was captured during the legendary Nigerian artist's final live show just 48 days before his death. Church Of Sound was founded in 2016 by Lex Blondin and Spencer Martin.…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Fine :: Jazz Dreams
aquariumdrunkard.description: For all the creativity Copenhagen’s avant-pop scene can offer, a lot of it had started to hang on its own clichés. Who knew it could be recharged by a blasé attitude and a good old dose of harmonic complexity? Fine’s Jazz Dreams is full of the kind of drowsy virtuosity that once again justifies the hype over that scene's prolific output; it's as if you were inhabiting the fantasies of a conservatory student who fell asleep in counterpoint class.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Tía Rosa :: Thirteen Automatic Dreams
aquariumdrunkard.description: Via Mexico City, Thirteen Automatic Dreams is the thrillingly comfy new record by Tía Rosa. Here is some minimalist kosmische with a Latin pop sensibility, a bridge between the noisy regularity of Neu! and the sugared melancholy of balada romántica. It all plays like a lost soundtrack to the Nevada desert of the Nocilla Trilogy , where shoes hang from a lonely poplar, or like Stereolab is being collectively hallucinated from one of those little Durango towns where Jodorowsky liked to film his deranged acid westerns.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sunday Mourners :: A-Rhythm Absolute
aquariumdrunkard.description: Skirting the edges of canonical post-punk, the debut record by four piece Sunday Mourners is a gripping, youthful art-rock explosion. There are distinct flashes tapping into Chairs Missing -era jagged melodicism here, VU at their most intractable jamming there (the twelve minute "Darling" a prime example). Above all, A-Rhythm Absolute is a downright lively listen, hitting all of the spirited guitar-centric benchmarks to make the listener a reinvigorated believer in the state of such a modern landscape.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Happy Thanksgiving :: Doug Sahm And Friends – Austin, TX 1972
aquariumdrunkard.description: Tradition runs rampant around Thanksgiving: generations of old recipes, football, Alice’s Restaurant, and, of course, a parade of balloons shutting down NYC. What else do you need? If you thought you were covered in the Thanksgiving tradition department, we did too…until a few years ago, when someone blew the dust off a long lost tape — Doug Sahm’s Thanksgiving Jam.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Yr Knives :: Begin Yr Singing
aquariumdrunkard.description: On a recent episode of Vish Khanna's Kreative Kontrol podcast, Douglas McCombs explained that music his his primary social activity. This explains the bassist's extensive resume, which includes Tortoise, Brokeback, BASIC, Black Duck, Eleventh Dream Day, and The Sea and Cake. With Chicago's Yr Knives, he adds yet another group to the mix. On the group's debut, Begin Yr Singing , he joins drummer Quin Kirchner and guitarists Brian J Sulpizio (Health & Beauty) and Andrew Trim for a wild ride that hypnotically blends progressive rock, free jazz, krautrock, and desert blues. If one were scrambling for a genre, you could select "post-rock," but could equally apply the even less loved term "jazz…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Trio Ternura :: A Gira / Razão De Ser
aquariumdrunkard.description: Trio Ternura—the Brazilian sibling group consisting of sisters Jussara and Jurema and brother Robson Ternura—has been receiving the reissue treatment via Madrid’s Vampisoul label since last year and we are absolutely here for it. Last year, they dished out a new pressing of the group’s 1973 single “A Gira” b/w “Last Tango in Paris.” The A-side is a polyrhythmic groove with tribal percussion and silky, chanting harmonies which finds itself paired with a glittery lounge rendering of Argentinean saxophonist Gato Barbieri’s Grammy-winning film score.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Larry Crane (Tape Op)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Today on Transmissions, a conversation with Larry Crane of Tape Op magazine. This year, Larry and Tape Op celebrated 30 years of creative advice with Making Music , a book that collects 26 of the best ever interviews from the magazine, including creators like Glyn Johns, Tony Visconti, RZA, Brian Eno, Joe Boyd, Lee “Scratch” Perry, and many more. It’s not just for recording aficionados, but it never skimps on glorious detail.

mubi.title: A World in Parts
mubi.description: The Journey (Peter Watkins, 1987). At Radio Canada, preparations are underway for Ronald Reagan’s 1985 summit with Canadian prime minister Brian Mulroney. Filmmaker Peter Watkins and his crew have been allowed into meetings where the broadcasters plan their coverage down to the second. Everyone must synchronize their watches: A discrepancy of 40 seconds, one participant warns, could throw off the day’s work. A shot requested at 17:02 might be missed if recorded 30 seconds later. “One thing is certain: there can’t be anything unexpected tonight,” another member of the team declares. Security officials will provide the presidential route, street by street, allowing the text to be prepared…

His filmography moves between intricate narratives rooted in political and crime thrillers, and deeply intimate and socially driven dramas. Trump. Abassi tells host Rico Gagliano about both, and what it was like to navigate two very different kinds of censorship. mubi.title: The Last Emperor: A Conversation with Jeremy Thomas

A list of filmmakers whose work makes up Thomas’s production portfolio reads like a who’s who of maverick visionaries, each of them fiercely loyal to the last: Nicolas Roeg and David Cronenberg; Takeshi Kitano and Jonathan Glazer; Nagisa Ōshima and Wim Wenders; Jerzy Skolimowski and Bernardo Bertolucci, whose The Last Emperor (1987) won Thomas the Academy Award for…
